label: adaptive-quality
note: Illustrative stated starting points; live provider calls, no user Chart writes.

context.intention: I maintain a consistent workout routine.
context.actualStartingPoint: I exercise sporadically. I can use three 30-minute slots each week for bodyweight exercise at home.
context.destinationDescription: I maintain a consistent workout routine.

analysis.startingPointSummary: They currently exercise sporadically and have three 30-minute slots each week available for bodyweight exercise at home.
assumptions: The intended routine is three home bodyweight workouts per week using the stated 30-minute slots.
No equipment, gym access, coaching or extra time is assumed.
The route focuses on observable routine, energy and body-readiness changes rather than medical outcomes.

routeDesign.complexityReason: This is a habit-building destination with a clear weekly time resource but inconsistent current follow-through.
routeDesign.countReason: The distinct achievements are a first workable week, a repeatable pattern, resilience when a week is imperfect, and a sustained self-directed rhythm.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: A first full week is feasible because the person already has three 30-minute home slots available.

raw.destination: Maintain a consistent three-times-a-week home workout routine

waypoints.title: Complete one workable workout week
waypoints.rationale: This proves the routine can fit into the time and setting they already have.
waypoints.completionCriteria: One week is complete with all three available 30-minute home workout slots used.
requirements: Three home bodyweight sessions completed in one week
Each session fits inside a 30-minute slot
At least one simple full-body movement pattern is used in each session

moves.title: Choose the three 30-minute slots for this week
moves.rationale: Using the time already available turns the intention into a visible place in the week.

moves.title: Pick five bodyweight moves for the first session
moves.rationale: A short list removes decision-making when the slot starts.

moves.title: Do the first 30-minute home session in the next chosen slot
moves.rationale: The routine begins when one real session happens, not when the whole plan is perfect.

moves.title: Repeat the same simple session in the other two slots
moves.rationale: Repetition helps the week feel manageable before adding variety.

waypoints.title: Make the week pattern repeatable
waypoints.rationale: Consistency becomes easier when the routine feels familiar instead of improvised each time.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Two consecutive weeks show the same workout pattern can be repeated without restarting from scratch.
requirements: Three home sessions completed in each of two consecutive weeks
The same weekly slots are used when possible
A familiar session structure is used without rebuilding the workout each time
The person can name how their body or energy feels after sessions

moves.title: Reuse the same three slots for the second week
moves.rationale: Keeping the timing stable makes the routine easier to recognize.

moves.title: Keep the same workout structure and adjust only one movement if needed
moves.rationale: Small adjustment protects repeatability while avoiding boredom or strain.

moves.title: After each session, note one word about energy or body feel
moves.rationale: Noticing the effect helps connect the routine to lived experience.

moves.title: At week’s end, keep what worked and remove one friction point
moves.rationale: A repeatable routine improves by reducing obstacles, not by adding complexity.

waypoints.title: Recover the routine during an imperfect week
waypoints.rationale: A consistent routine needs a way to continue when a slot is missed, delayed or low-energy.
waypoints.completionCriteria: One imperfect week is handled without abandoning the workout routine.
requirements: A missed, delayed or low-energy slot is met with a specific adjustment
The next workout happens instead of waiting for a fresh start
At least one session uses a reduced version when needed
The week still contains visible movement rather than becoming a skipped week

moves.title: Decide the smallest acceptable version of a 30-minute session
moves.rationale: A reduced version gives the routine a way to survive low-energy days.

moves.title: If a planned slot is missed, choose the next available home slot that week
moves.rationale: Rescheduling quickly prevents one miss from becoming a full stop.

moves.title: Use the reduced version once instead of skipping when energy is low
moves.rationale: Maintaining the thread matters more than making every session ideal.

moves.title: Return to the normal 30-minute session at the next planned slot
moves.rationale: The routine becomes resilient when it can bend and then resume.

waypoints.title: Sustain the routine without restarting
waypoints.rationale: The destination is reached when workouts are part of normal life rather than a short push.
waypoints.completionCriteria: The home workout routine holds for a month with self-directed planning and recovery from small interruptions.
requirements: Four consecutive weeks include regular home bodyweight workouts
The person chooses each week’s three workout slots without rebuilding the habit
Missed or difficult sessions are adjusted without stopping the routine
The routine feels recognizable in the body, energy and weekly rhythm

moves.title: At the start of each week, place the three workout slots
moves.rationale: A short weekly decision keeps the routine active without overplanning.

moves.title: Use one familiar workout structure for most sessions
moves.rationale: Familiarity lowers the effort needed to begin.

moves.title: Keep one reduced session option available every week
moves.rationale: A built-in fallback protects consistency during tired or crowded days.

moves.title: After four weeks, identify the timing and session style that worked best
moves.rationale: Naming the working pattern helps the routine continue on its own.

suggestedOneMove.title: Choose the three 30-minute slots for this week
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Using the time already available turns the intention into a visible place in the week.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Use the three home slots as the anchor; the early aim is not intensity, but making the routine recognizable in your week.

context.intention: I successfully complete my first half marathon.
context.actualStartingPoint: I run 5 km comfortably twice a week. I can train three days each week. I have never completed a half marathon.
context.destinationDescription: I successfully complete my first half marathon.

analysis.startingPointSummary: Runs 5 km comfortably twice a week, can train three days each week, no prior half marathon completion.
assumptions: Current 5 km comfortable pace provides a solid base to build weekly distance safely.
Three available training days per week are sufficient for gradual distance accumulation.

routeDesign.complexityReason: Progressing from a 5 km base to a 21.1 km half marathon requires building endurance capacity, adapting to longer weekly long runs, and managing recovery.
routeDesign.countReason: Three distinct physical adaptations needed: extending weekly distance beyond 10 km, building sustained endurance for distance progression, and completing the full 21.1 km event.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: Completing a continuous run distance exceeding the current 5 km baseline.

raw.destination: I successfully complete my first half marathon.

waypoints.title: Establish a reliable 10 km distance capability
waypoints.rationale: Doubling the current comfortable distance proves aerobic capacity can support longer efforts.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Complete a continuous 10 km run during weekly training.

moves.title: Add one kilometre to the weekly long run
moves.rationale: Gradually stretches endurance without overloading joints.

moves.title: Maintain the two regular 5 km runs as maintenance efforts
moves.rationale: Preserves aerobic base while the long run increases.

moves.title: Run a continuous 8 km test effort
moves.rationale: Validates the halfway transition toward the 10 km milestone.

moves.title: Complete a continuous 10 km run
moves.rationale: Reaches the baseline threshold for distance progression.

waypoints.title: Build a consistent 15 km long run base
waypoints.rationale: Reaching 15 km prepares the body and routine for race-distance fatigue.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Complete a continuous 15 km training run with stable recovery.

moves.title: Extend the weekly long run to 12 km
moves.rationale: Builds upon the 10 km milestone safely.

moves.title: Incorporate a recovery walk or rest day after the long run
moves.rationale: Ensures energy levels remain stable across the three training days.

moves.title: Run a continuous 14 km effort
moves.rationale: Tests physical readiness just beneath the 15 km target.

moves.title: Complete a continuous 15 km run
moves.rationale: Establishes the endurance threshold needed for the final training block.

waypoints.title: Complete the 21.1 km half marathon distance
waypoints.rationale: Fulfills the final event completion through race-day execution.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Successfully complete a 21.1 km half marathon distance.

moves.title: Plan the final tapering schedule across the three training days
moves.rationale: Reduces accumulated fatigue prior to the event.

moves.title: Review hydration and nutrition routines during a 16 km run
moves.rationale: Identifies fueling requirements for longer exertion.

moves.title: Complete the 21.1 km half marathon
moves.rationale: Achieves the intended destination.

suggestedOneMove.title: Add one kilometre to the weekly long run
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Starts the gradual distance expansion from your current 5 km baseline.

context.actualStartingPoint: Anchor is launched with 20 paying users. I am the solo developer, with 10 hours a week for growth and no paid advertising budget. I can contact current users and have subscription analytics.

vision.title: A sustainable Anchor business
vision.description: 10,000 paying users who continue using Anchor

analysis.startingPointSummary: Anchor is launched with 20 paying users, operated by a solo developer with 10 hours a week, no paid ad budget, and access to current users and subscription analytics.
assumptions: Growth relies entirely on organic acquisition channels and retention of existing users.
The 10-hour weekly time limit remains constant throughout the route.

routeDesign.complexityReason: Scaling from 20 to 10,000 paying users without a budget requires sequential achievement of retention, a repeatable organic channel, and operational capacity.
routeDesign.countReason: Four distinct operational states separate the starting point from 10,000 paying users.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: Current user feedback and retention data analyzed to identify core value drivers.

waypoints.title: Analyze and stabilize user retention
waypoints.rationale: Understanding why current users stay ensures the product retains value before expanding acquisition.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Cohort retention stabilizes at or above 80% over a 30-day period.

moves.title: Review subscription analytics for the 20 current users
moves.rationale: Identify usage patterns among active subscribers.

moves.title: Email 5 current users to ask why they use Anchor
moves.rationale: Gather direct qualitative feedback on product value.

moves.title: Identify the primary feature used by retained customers
moves.rationale: Pinpoint the core value driver to protect during growth.

waypoints.title: Establish one repeatable organic acquisition channel
waypoints.rationale: A solo developer without an ad budget needs a reliable, non-paid method to bring in prospective users.
waypoints.completionCriteria: One functional organic acquisition channel consistently brings in new signups each week.

moves.title: Select one organic channel matching available skills
moves.rationale: Choose between content, community outreach, or direct networking.

moves.title: Draft three informational posts or direct outreach messages
moves.rationale: Prepare initial material to test the chosen channel.

moves.title: Publish or send the first batch of outreach
moves.rationale: Initiate contact with potential users through the chosen method.

waypoints.title: Reach 500 paying users
waypoints.rationale: Reaching 500 paying users proves the acquisition channel and retention mechanics work at a larger scale.

moves.title: Allocate weekly hours specifically to organic outreach
moves.rationale: Maintain a consistent posting or contact schedule.

moves.title: Track conversion rates from the acquisition channel
moves.rationale: Monitor how many prospects convert to paying users.

moves.title: Refine onboarding messaging based on new user questions
moves.rationale: Remove friction points for incoming signups.

waypoints.title: Reach 10,000 paying users
waypoints.rationale: Scaling the proven organic and retention engine to the final destination.

moves.title: Automate onboarding email sequences for new signups
moves.rationale: Save time while maintaining user engagement.

moves.title: Scale weekly content or outreach output within the 10-hour limit
moves.rationale: Increase efficiency of the acquisition channel.

moves.title: Monitor churn metrics as volume increases
moves.rationale: Ensure retention holds steady at scale.

suggestedOneMove.title: Review subscription analytics for the 20 current users
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Start by examining existing usage data to understand current retention.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Focus on stabilizing retention and finding one repeatable organic channel within your 10-hour weekly limit.
